## Completion Report

**Questions asked & answered**: 5 of 5 (2 decided by you, 3 delegated to my judgement)

**Updated spec**: `specs/002-password-reset/spec.md`

**Decisions recorded**:
1. A successful `reset` unlocks the account and clears its failed-login tally; both new commands work on a locked account.
2. A successful `passwd` cancels an outstanding token.
3. *(delegated)* Overlapping invocations stay out of scope, no locking added; single use guaranteed between non-overlapping runs, store integrity guaranteed regardless.
4. *(delegated)* `--ttl` ceiling of 86400 s; above it is a usage error, exit 2 — not silently clamped.
5. *(delegated)* `reset-token` prints the token alone, no expiry line (no change to FR-032).

**Sections touched**: Context; Clarifications (new); User Story 1 scenarios; User Story 2 (title, narrative, independent test, scenarios); Edge Cases; Functional Requirements — FR-033, FR-036b, FR-036c, FR-038, FR-041 revised and **FR-038a**, **FR-038b** added; Key Entities; Success Criteria — SC-011, SC-012 revised and **SC-020** added; Assumptions.

**Spec Quality Checklist**: 16/16 → 16/16 items passing, no state changes. I updated its Notes to record the re-validation and to widen the scope note: FR-041's freeze on the five existing commands is now "everything a user can see, plus no token-state effect other than `passwd` cancelling and `delete` discarding". Both are invisible to existing output and assertions, so SC-010 holds unchanged.

**Coverage summary**:

| Category | Status |
|---|---|
| Functional Scope & Behavior | Clear |
| Domain & Data Model | Resolved — token lifecycle now has exactly four end routes plus expiry (FR-038a, SC-020) |
| Interaction & UX Flow | Resolved — locked-account recovery in three commands; output contract confirmed |
| Non-Functional: Security | Resolved — lifetime ceiling, token retired on password change |
| Non-Functional: Performance / Reliability | Clear — SC-018 and FR-038b |
| Non-Functional: Observability | Outstanding (low impact) — no audit record of a reset; the tool has no logging, FR-044 and the no-hidden-I/O constraint forbid writing elsewhere, and no command could read it back, so it would be untestable under Principle III |
| Integration & External Dependencies | Clear — none; stdlib only |
| Edge Cases & Failure Handling | Resolved — concurrency and `--ttl` bounds |
| Constraints & Tradeoffs | Clear |
| Terminology & Consistency | Clear |
| Completion Signals | Clear |
| Misc / Placeholders | Clear — no TODOs, no unquantified adjectives |

**Deferred to planning**: whether a spent token's record is purged from the account or kept marked-used. The two are observably identical through the CLI, so it is a storage decision for `/speckit-plan`, not a spec one.

Nothing outstanding blocks planning — the one Outstanding item is unimplementable by design rather than undecided.
